consensus_summary: Sand primarily signifies an innumerable multitude and, in the building parable, an unstable or inadequate foundation. Other context-dependent senses are also recognized.
book_summary: Sand signifies a countless multitude; as a foundation, it represents the instability of relying on a crowd of people not joined by covenant rather than on the covenant Rock.
consensus_core_identification: Innumerable multitude; secondarily, an unstable foundation.
book_core_identification: Countless multitude; when foundational, an unstable crowd outside covenant in contrast with Rock.
boundary_disagreement: The broad identifications match, but the book specifically reclassifies the foundation image as reliance on an uncovenanted crowd. The consensus instead associates Matthew 7 more generally with hearing without obedience or any inadequate foundation and does not impose the crowd/covenant boundary.
material_contradiction: There is no contradiction at the minimum core: both identify multitude and foundational instability. The book's covenant-crowd explanation is a materially narrower interpretive specification rather than a replacement of those core meanings.
rationale: The multitude sense directly matches the consensus, and the unstable-foundation sense is also recognized by all responses. The entry is REFINED because it connects these senses and gives the sand-foundation a specific human and covenantal referent not contained in the consensus formulation.
strongest_objection: Genesis 22:17, Hosea 1:10, and Revelation 20:8 strongly support innumerability, while Matthew 7:26 supports an unsuccessful sand foundation. However, Matthew identifies the foolish builder as one who hears Jesus' sayings and does not do them; it does not itself identify the sand as a crowd, uncovenanted people, or the opposite of a covenant Rock.
